extracted.intended_audience: journalists, researchers, fact-checkers, and policy analysts tracking disinformation and deceptive news websites
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and examples for identifying and documenting deceptive, spoof, or state-linked news websites (including use of generative AI, spoofing, copied content, fabricated media, and indicators of operator links). Useful for researchers compiling lists of problematic news homepages.

rubrics_metrics.name: State-sponsored support / operator links
rubrics_metrics.description: The operator (John Mark Dougan) is described as receiving financial and material resources from Russia's primary intelligence agency, the GRU, to assist with the websites, with the goal of providing disinformation to the American public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use evidence of funding, material support, or explicit ties to state intelligence services (e.g., GRU-provided resources, funding from institutes linked to Aleksandr Dugin) as an indicator that a site is part of a state-linked disinformation effort. Note third-party characterizations (e.g., NewsGuard calling an operator a 'Russian operative') as corroborating context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of generative AI to create disinformation
rubrics_metrics.description: One resource used by the operator is a generative AI tool that creates disinformation in the form of plausible social media posts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag sites when there is direct evidence researchers or governments cite use of generative AI (e.g., AI-generated social posts, AI-rewritten articles). Examples include sites whose article titles or bodies contain LLM prompts or researchers' notes that content was produced with a large language model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scale of linked domain network (CopyCop)
rubrics_metrics.description: As of May 2024, at least 167 website domains, dubbed 'CopyCop', are likely linked to the same operator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document the number and patterns of related domains as an indicator of an organized campaign. Large counts of similar or related domains suggest an orchestrated network rather than isolated bad actors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spoofing established outlets (name/logo mimicry)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sites that spoof established newspapers or broadcasters (e.g., 'bbc-uk.news' spoofing the BBC, Chicago Chronicle, Houston Post, New York Daily News, San Francisco Chronicle, Arizona Observer).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify deliberate mimicry of well-known outlet names, logos, or branding. Spoofing can be signaled by near-identical names, fake logos, or claims of historical continuity that contradict registration data.

rubrics_metrics.name: False claims about site history / fabricated provenance
rubrics_metrics.description: Sites asserting false founding dates or histories (e.g., a site claiming to have been in existence since 1937 while actually registered in February 2024).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare site 'About' pages and claimed provenance with WHOIS/registration data. Discrepancies indicate attempts to fabricate legitimacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impersonation of political organizations / election manipulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Sites that promoted an impostor site of a political party (e.g., a fake Renaissance Party site that falsely claimed it would pay citizens to vote).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag sites that create impostor political pages or make false campaign-related claims, especially around elections — these indicate attempts to influence voters or manipulate political discourse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reposting or rewriting content from legitimate news sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Many articles were reposted from other websites or rewritten from legitimate outlets (e.g., attempts to rewrite articles from Le Parisien, 20 Minutes, Libération, Le Figaro, Le Monde, La Croix).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detect copy/repost behavior by comparing articles against known source publications. Rewriting (including via LLMs) of legitimate reporting is an indicator of low-originality, deceptive aggregation, or content-farm behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence of LLM prompt artifacts in articles
rubrics_metrics.description: Some article titles or content include prompts for large language models, indicating machine-assisted or machine-produced content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for prompt-like strings, unnatural phrasing, or explicit prompt text in titles or bodies. Presence of prompt artifacts is a strong indicator of generative-AI involvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fabricated multimedia (e.g., fabricated audio)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sites accused by authorities of publishing fabricated audio of conversations between officials (e.g., fabricated audio of U.S. officials).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat fabricated audio or other manipulated multimedia as high-severity manipulative content. Verify provenance, consult forensic analyses, and note government or research findings alleging fabrication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct copying or plagiarism from major outlets
rubrics_metrics.description: Some sites copied articles directly from major outlets (e.g., copying ABC News and CBS News content).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detect exact or near-exact copying; this indicates either content theft or automated scraping/aggregation. Copied content without attribution supports classification as deceptive or low-quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imitation of local TV/newscast brands
rubrics_metrics.description: Sites that imitate local TV stations or local broadcast branding (e.g., KBSF-San Francisco News imitating a local news TV station).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local-TV-style branding used by non-broadcasters can be an impersonation tactic to gain trust. Check broadcast affiliations and station licensing/ownership for verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of demonstrably false claims about public figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Sites published and spread false claims about public figures (e.g., false claims about Kamala Harris or Volodymyr Zelenskyy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and document clear factual falsehoods about individuals, cross-check with reputable fact-checkers and primary sources. Repeated false claims about public figures indicate disinformation intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poor/no contact information and placeholder content
rubrics_metrics.description: Sites lacking valid contact info or containing placeholder text (e.g., 'About' pages containing Lorem ipsum).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absence of credible contact details or presence of placeholder text suggests the site is not a professionally maintained news outlet. Use WHOIS, About, and contact pages to corroborate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign-language or metadata clues (e.g., image filenames)
rubrics_metrics.description: Site artifacts such as image filenames in a foreign language (e.g., Russian filenames) that suggest a foreign operational origin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspect image names, metadata, hosting location, language artifacts, and code comments for clues about authorship or origin. These technical indicators can corroborate other evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Researchers' and official attributions (third-party assessments)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sites or networks noted by researchers, Digital Forensic Research Labs, or governments as likely using LLMs or being part of campaigns (e.g., Atlantic Council DFRLab conclusions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weight independent researcher reports and official government attributions heavily. Explicit findings (e.g., DFRLab concluding LLM use) provide robust evidence for classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Network evolution / defunct domains
rubrics_metrics.description: Some entries in the list are marked 'Defunct', indicating domains may be taken down or abandoned over time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track status changes over time; defunct domains can indicate tactical rotation or fall-off. Maintain historical records and note when domains become inactive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-campaign content reuse (Doppelganger/Dubbed campaign reuse)
rubrics_metrics.description: Many articles were reposted from a website used in other campaigns (e.g., Russia's 'Doppelganger' campaign), indicating reuse across operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify content reuse across multiple domains or campaigns; cross-posting of the same false narratives across a set of domains supports classification as coordinated activity.
